note: The Java engine, which replayed 0.16.0 run for run up to 1.0.0; 1.1.0 changes only how the cost counts autoscaled parts and prices the peak (ADR-0074); 1.1.1 measures the base's per-request rates in the buckets nearest it when none is at it; 1.2.0 prices a third-party API without a price at its technology preset's price, or leaves it out of the month (ADR-0081); 1.2.1 counts a cache's refused lookups in its hit ratio and words the advice on a failing cache by what its callers lack (ADR-0082); 1.3.0 reports a database's busiest instance's CPU and sets its CPU ceiling where that instance fills (ADR-0083); 1.4.0 counts lost messages against availability and judges a message's age (ADR-0084); 1.5.0 sizes a Kafka broker from the Kafka experiment's measurements and reports idle consumers (ADR-0085); 1.5.1 counts a commit's log flush as a wait in the instant estimate, not as database CPU, which changes no simulated knee (ADR-0089); 1.5.2 spreads a cache's commands over every shard's cores in the instant estimate and counts a read-through cache's fills in its slots and CPU, which changes no simulated knee either (ADR-0092). Not frozen yet: its source trees (archsim-engine, archsim-model, archsim-cli) are pinned when it is frozen, before the next held-out campaign.

1.6.0 counts the vCPUs of a service, database or cache with 2 or more vCPU as hyperthread pairs at a sibling speed of 0.6 by default from schema 1.11, and as whole cores on an instance family whose vCPUs are whole cores, on a serverless platform and as pods on Kubernetes; auto-sizing sizes a part for the kind of vCPU its instance type gives it; and the instant estimate saturates a part on its own hyperthread pairs where its vCPUs fill at the sibling speed, at any load, and runs an overloaded one's work at that speed, where it extrapolated from the speed at the peak and, past its vCPUs, counted them taking turns at its own work too, and the design review judges such a part's CPU by the share of that ceiling its work takes, as the estimate does, and says so, where it judged it at the speed at the peak and called that share busy, so at 0.6 it said nothing from about 80% to 93% of the ceiling (ADR-0091). A design saved before 1.11, the benchmark harness's among them (schemas 1.0 and 1.7), is pinned to whole cores, so no simulated knee moves. It is counted as tuned on all nine experiments measured so far, the first held-out set's among them, since the change was made with their results in view; the second held-out set, registered before it (ADR-0090), stays held out. With it the benchmark harness fits the service's CPU per request as a law of its rate, floor + shared x rate^-k, carried above the calibration staircase to where the service's CPUs fill but no further than twice the top rate, where it held the top rate's cost flat (ADR-0093): a model change that leaves the engine's results as they were, in-sample on all nine, which moved cache-aside's median knee error over its counted v6 runs from -22% to -7%, cache-ttl's from -6% to +10%, chain's from +30% to +37%, Kafka's from -3% to +7% and pg-mixed's from +16% to +19%, and the median of the 37 runs' absolute errors from 16.3% to 12.9%. Its predicted range is fitted on all nine experiments it is tuned on, with the model's error as one each experiment's runs share (0.32) and one each run has (0), where it was one error fitted on the four tuned-on experiments (0.15): leaving out each experiment, the 80% range holds 41 of the 49 counted runs, where the earlier error held 32, every miss below the range (ADR-0094). Its benchmark designs run on the laptop's host machine as its contention checks fit it unless BENCH_HOST=off, where they ran on it only with BENCH_HOST=on: a model change that leaves the engine's results as they were, which, in-sample on the 37 counted v6 runs, takes the runs whose knee is predicted too high from 25 to 4 and the largest over-prediction of an experiment's median from +72% to +16%, and the median of the runs' absolute errors from 12.9% to 14.5%, cache-aside's median falling to -29%; the range refitted on its knees holds 37 of the 49 counted runs leaving out each experiment, 10 of its 12 misses above the range; and a freeze names the host machine's fit by its digest, hostFit (ADR-0095). Frozen on 2026-11-20 (tag engine-1.6.0), its designs on the laptop's host machine as the committed contention checks fit it (hostFit), to predict the second held-out set (ADR-0088, ADR-0090).

1.6.1 places evenly spaced arrivals where the offered rate, added up since the last, reaches one more request, where 1.6.0 took the gap to the next from the rate at the last arrival, so a ramp or a trace that starts at 0 now sends its requests from the start. The benchmark designs run at constant rates, where the gaps are 1.6.0's to the bit, so no simulated knee moves; the inputs, the range and the host fit stay 1.6.0's, and so does tunedOn. Not frozen.

1.6.2 counts a queue's deliveries alone in its holding time, where 1.6.1 also counted each publish from its start to its acknowledgement, so a queue's capacity, its formulas and its finding on what it can sustain follow from how long a message holds a consumer (ADR-0117). Every event of a simulation is as it was, so no simulated knee moves; the inputs, the range and the host fit stay 1.6.0's, and so does tunedOn. Not frozen.
